## tl;dr

I used my own Python tool over 1000 times. 
What did I learn?

## 

I [wrote about jot before](), my opinionated Python command-line tool for jotting down little timestamped notes to myself.

If you've read this blog, you know I make things and... move on.

Guess what?
I actually used this one consistently.

In fact, I've been jotting every work day since August 2025 and have banked over 1000 jottings.

How has this been useful?
I write weeknotes and timesheets every Friday afternoon.
But I can't usually remember stuff.
So this has beena good 'brain outside my brain'.

Also, it's nearly time for my annual appraisal. 
Normally I struggle to remember what I've done.
Not just the major things, but also the little things that fall through the cracks.

Which are often the things that actually matter.
To me.
And to my colleagues.

I helped unblock things.
I reviewed loads of tiny pull requests.
I spent some time learning about something.

The jot file has helped me record and recognise these things.
And, crucially, reflect on them.

I've also used it to jot down when I've received unsolicited feedback.
Turns out I've been useful to people.
Who knew?
I certainly didn't before I started writing these things down.

Is jot a world-beating bit of software?
Ahahaha, no.
Has it made a difference to me?
Aye, it has.

## 

I started developing jot to learn how to Python and write CLIs.
That is definitely a success.

The culmination of that is a tool I use daily, yes.
But the true final boss is to upload it to PyPi.

Well... jot is now available on PyPi.
Install like regular person with:


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
pip install jot-cli
```
:::


And then follow the docs and use it like:


::: {.cell}

```{.bash .cell-code}
jot "ate an apple"
```
:::
